title: The Housemaid
synopsis: You took the live-in housekeeping job because nobody else would hire someone with your record. The Winchesters' attic locks from the outside. You'll find out why.

nodes.text: The house is bigger than the brochure suggested. Mrs. Winchester smiles from the doorway like a woman who has practiced. Her husband Andrew loads your duffel into the foyer himself.

choices.text: Be cheerful and grateful
Be polite and observant

nodes.text: Nina Winchester guides you through twelve rooms she does not appear to know. Andrew lingers a step behind. The attic stairs are at the end of the upstairs hall. She does not turn that light on.

choices.text: Ask about the attic directly
choices.consequence: Curiosity gets you fired or hired.

choices.text: Note it silently and move on

nodes.text: Nina hands you a typed list of rules. Twenty-three of them. Rule eleven: 'Do not enter the attic for any reason.' Rule twelve: 'You will sleep in the attic.'

choices.text: Sign and ask no questions
Ask gentle, clarifying questions

nodes.text: The attic is hot and small and the door locks from the outside. The lock looks new. You hear, downstairs, a marriage that is not whispered enough.

choices.text: Try the door to see if it really locks
choices.consequence: Test the trap before it tests you.

choices.text: Sit very still and listen

nodes.text: Cecelia, nine, is the only person in this house who acts like she sees you. She is, you sense immediately, both clever and afraid. She slides you a folded paper at breakfast.

choices.text: Read the note when alone
Burn the note and never speak of it
choices.consequence: Some kindnesses must be turned down for safety.

nodes.text: Andrew finds reasons to be in your kitchen. He compliments your coffee, your hair, your record. He has read your file. He makes 'I know what you did' sound like a love note.

choices.text: Hold a hard line on professional distance
choices.consequence: Distance is a vow you keep with both hands.

choices.text: Pretend to laugh along while building a plan

nodes.text: Nina cries in the pantry over a broken jar. It is not about the jar. She wants to tell you something and then visibly decides not to. The decision costs her.

choices.text: Gently invite her to talk
Bring her tea and listen
choices.consequence: Silence can be more useful than questions.

nodes.text: You find an old payroll stub jammed behind a drawer — the name of the maid before you. You search her online. She, you discover, has been missing for fourteen months.

choices.text: Photograph the stub and hide the photo
Reach out to the missing maid's family

nodes.text: There is a room on the second floor neither Winchester ever enters. The door is locked, but not securely. A key hangs in plain sight on a hook in the kitchen.

choices.text: Take the key and look inside
Wait until you understand the house better

nodes.text: Nina pulls you into the laundry room and whispers: 'He's done it before. He's done it to me. I need you to help me. I need you not to think I'm crazy.' Her wrist has finger marks shaped like a man's hand.

choices.text: Trust her and plan together
Trust her and contact a lawyer for her first

nodes.text: The locked room turns out to be ordinary. The interesting room is the cellar. Boxes labeled with women's names. The dates on them are spread over a decade.

choices.text: Photograph everything quickly
choices.consequence: Build a case without being seen.

choices.text: Take one box upstairs and confront

nodes.text: You go to the local sheriff at lunch. He listens. He nods. He calls Andrew Winchester 'Andy' and tells you 'we'll handle it.' You realize you may have just announced yourself to the wrong room.

choices.text: Skip town with Nina tonight
Find a different jurisdiction

nodes.text: Cecelia's room has a nanny cam pointed at the door. You realize the cam is wired through Andrew's office. You also realize the cam can be turned around.

choices.text: Turn it on the master bedroom
Smash it and pretend it broke

nodes.text: The power goes out in a thunderstorm. Andrew, on the stairs, voice changed, says, 'You have nowhere to go.' He is wrong but you have minutes to prove it.

choices.text: Get Nina and Cecelia to the car
Lure Andrew to the attic and lock him in

nodes.text: Nina's college friend — a divorce attorney with a particular reputation — meets you both in a hotel lobby. She has, she says, been waiting six years for Nina to call. She has been ready for six years.

choices.text: Sign the paperwork; start the protective orders
Push for criminal charges immediately

nodes.text: Three of you in a car at 2 a.m. Cecelia asleep in the back. Nina holding a list of motels with cash. You driving like a person who has been preparing to leave somewhere her entire life.

choices.text: Drive across state lines tonight
Stop at a women's shelter you trust

nodes.text: Andrew, in the attic, banging on the door he installed for someone else. You stand in the hall with Cecelia's hand in yours. You realize the lock has, in fact, always been on his side. He just hadn't tested it.

choices.text: Call 911 from the bottom of the stairs
Walk out the front door with the women
choices.consequence: The trap is now his alone.

nodes.text: The county prosecutor in the next state takes your file and your photos seriously. She has been looking for a Winchester case for years. The boxes in the cellar matter. So does your testimony.

choices.text: Agree to testify fully
Negotiate witness protection first

nodes.text: By morning Cecelia has her own bed, Nina has her own door, and you are sitting at a table with bad coffee and three other women who have, in different houses, been you. Nobody has to explain anything.

choices.text: Help Nina start over
choices.consequence: Be the friend the last maid didn't have.

choices.text: Decide you need to start over too
choices.consequence: Survivors are allowed their own road.

nodes.text: It takes a year. Andrew is convicted. Nina sells the house. Cecelia gets a therapist she likes. The boxes in the cellar each become a charge.

choices.text: Stay close to the family
choices.consequence: Family is sometimes the people who carried each other.

choices.text: Move on with what you learned

nodes.text: Cecelia, eighteen, finds you at a college fair. She is okay. She wants to study law. She has, in her hand, a small framed photo of the three of you on that morning at the shelter. She wanted you to have it.

choices.text: Take the photo and the goodbye
choices.consequence: Some children's gifts are also closure.

choices.text: Take her to dinner and stay in her life

nodes.text: You don't become her mother. You become something close to an aunt, a witness, a steady person on speed dial. Nina remarries kindly. Cecelia grows up. The attic door is on the wrong side of the country and you sleep, finally, with both ears.

You start a small nonprofit — domestic workers' rights, an emergency line, a network. The next time a house like that hires someone like you, that someone has somewhere to call. The Winchesters became, accidentally, the seed of a much better thing.
